title: incident-symphony-runbook-and-notice-kit
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview:

This page defines the 'Incident Symphony' playbook: a prescriptive orchestration pattern for multi-team incidents where coordinated, time-boxed work and clear comms keep customers informed while engineers restore service. It pairs a lightweight role choreography with templates (status page + customer notices), concrete first-responder commands, and a repeatable game-day scenario to validate readiness.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, service owners, product on-call, support leads, oncall engineers.
- Applies to: service outages and degradations affecting production inference, embeddings, or API availability across hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Not for: low-level CI/CD failures that do not affect customer traffic.

Key principles:
- Clear roles and short cadence: assign a Conductor (IC equivalent) within 3 minutes of a page.
- Communication-first: aim to publish a status update within 10 minutes for any P2+ event.
- Contain then remediate: focus first on customer impact surface (routes, rate limiting, fallbacks), then identify root cause.
- Keep changes reversible: prefer routing changes and configuration toggles over destructive fixes during incident.

Severity table (quick reference):
|| Severity || Customer impact || SLA risk || Typical response || Time-to-first-update ||
|| Sev 1 || Total outage for > 1% customers or majority of requests failing || High || Bridge + IC + Exec notice || 10 minutes ||
|| Sev 2 || Partial service degradation (latency spikes, increased errors) || Medium || Triage + containment plan || 15 minutes ||
|| Sev 3 || Isolated error, single-region, nonblocking || Low || Owner-led fix || 60 minutes ||

Roles (musical metaphor):
- Conductor (Incident Commander): single point for decisions and customer-facing updates.
- Section Leads (Service Owners): one per impacted service (eg. runtime, routing, database).
- Instrument Leads (Engineers): hands-on triage and mitigation for a slice of the system.
- Scorekeeper (Scribe): records timeline, actions, and publishes postmortem draft skeleton.
- Audience & Comms (CSR/Liaison): crafts status page and customer notices.

Triage checklist (first 0-15 minutes):
1. Acknowledge the pager and declare the incident in Slack #ops-emergency.
2. Conductor creates the incident channel and pins this runbook.
3. Section Leads join and report an initial hypothesis in the channel.
4. Scorekeeper begins a timeline document and copies the Incident Summary template below.
5. Publish an initial status page entry (see templates).

Immediate actions (containment patterns):
- High latency / token amplification: temporarily route heavy customers to lower-seq-length model variant, enable prefix cache.
- Model OOMs / GPU failures: evict affected worker pool, scale up standby pool, enable routing fallback to CPU-quantized model.
- Persistent 5xx from runtime: set autoscale burst to 0 and route to healthy region; if global, initiate circuit-breaker to degrade non-critical routes (embeddings batch jobs).
- Excessive KV cache misses: restart cache proxy with warmup mode, throttle internal replays.

Runbook commands (examples):
- Check service pods and recent restarts:
  kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=runtime -o wide
  kubectl -n redwood describe pod <pod-name>
- Inspect GPU node health:
  redwoodctl nodes status --region us-west-2 --filter gpus
- Query error-rate from tracing backend (example):
  curl -s 'https://observability/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_requests_total{job=runtime,error!=""}[5m])' | jq
- Extract recent model load errors from logs:
  rg "Model load failed|KV cache corruption" /var/log/runtime/*.log | tail -n 200

Rollback and routing safe-play actions:
1. Prefer routing changes that are explicitly reversible: scale policy, model alias switch, region preference.
2. Example alias switch (imaginary CLI):
  redwoodctl routing set-alias model:prod:model-v2 model-v1 --reason "fallback for latency spike" --author $ME
3. Canary rollback pattern: route 10% traffic for 10 minutes, observe tail latency and 5xx ratio, then expand or rollback.

Escalation matrix (timeboxes):
- 0-10m: declare incident, initial update (Conductor).
- 10-30m: if no containment achieved, escalate to Platform SRE lead and open executive thread.
- 30-60m: if customer impact continues, prepare external customer notice (CSR lead) and schedule Exec update.

Status page templates (copy/paste and fill placeholders):
- Investigating:
  Title: "Investigating — Elevated error rates affecting inference API"
  Body: "We are investigating elevated errors for the Inference API affecting some requests in us-west-2. Our engineers are actively diagnosing the issue. Impact: some requests return 5xx or experience delayed responses. Next update: in 10 minutes. Workaround: retry with exponential backoff.
  
- Degraded / Partial outage:
  Title: "Partial degradation — Inference latency increased"
  Body: "We identified a service degradation impacting latency for text-generation requests for a subset of customers. We have reduced traffic to the affected worker pool and enabled fallback model variants while we remediate. Impact: increased latency up to XXs for affected requests. Next update: in 30 minutes.
  
- Resolved:
  Title: "Resolved — Inference API"
  Body: "The underlying issue has been resolved and normal service has been restored. Root cause: <summary>. Mitigation: <actions>. We will publish a post-incident report within 72 hours.

Customer notice email (short form):
Subject: Service degradation affecting Redwood inference — update
Hi <Customer>,
We wanted to let you know we are experiencing elevated errors/latency impacting the Inference API in <region>. Our team is actively working to resolve this and we have implemented fallback routing to reduce impact. We will follow up with a full post-incident summary. If you have an active outage, please reply to this message and we will prioritize.

Game-day scenario (exercise):
Objective: validate multi-region restoration and communications under a synthetic backend failure that triggers failover and routing changes.
Preconditions: standby region with 2 healthy worker pools, canary model variant available, synthetic traffic generator configured.
Steps:
1. At T0 simulate a GPU node retirement in primary region.
2. Observe autoscaler behavior and routing changes.
3. Conductor times to first update and validates status page publishing.
4. Section Leads perform a safe alias switch to canary, then measure error-rate and latency.
Scoring rubric:
- Publish initial status update within 10m: 10 points
- Containment (restore <5xx to baseline) within 30m: 20 points
- Successful reversible routing change without data loss: 30 points
- Post-exercise postmortem drafted within 48h: 10 points

Postmortem template (to be filled by Scorekeeper):
- Title and incident id
- Summary (1–2 sentences)
- Impact (customers affected, runtime window, quantifiable metrics)
- Timeline (minute-resolution actions and decisions)
- Root cause analysis (why the change happened and underlying systemic gap)
- Corrective actions (short, medium, long-term) with owners and due dates
- Validation plan (how we will prove the fixes work; include metrics and test plans)
- Lessons learned and follow-ups

On-call rotation & handoff checklist:
- Handoff should include: active incidents, muted alerts, known degradation, outstanding rollouts, and upcoming maintenance.
- Recommended shift length: 7 calendar days per on-call (primary), with 24-hour overlap handoff window on day 1 and day 7.
- Shadowing requirement: new on-call should shadow 3 rotations before taking primary.
- Handover message template (Slack pinned):
  - Current status: <OK/Degraded/Incident>
  - Active incidents: <id + brief>
  - Runbooks/links: <links>
  - Known flaps: <services>

Post-incident verification (72h):
- Owner runs the validation plan and reports pass/fail in the postmortem.
- Observability team runs a targeted alert sweep for anomaly recurrence.

Attachments and links:
- Dashboard: https://observability/dashboards/inference-slo
- Incident template: /confluence/templates/incident-timeline
- Routing CLI docs: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/routing-cli

Appendix — common quick fixes (copyable snippets):
- Clear KV proxy cache and warm:
  redis-cli -h kv-proxy flushall && curl -X POST https://internal/kv-warmup
- Temporarily increase concurrency for model pool:
  redwoodctl pools update runtime-v2 --concurrency 128 --region us-east-1

Notes and governance:
- All Sev 1 incidents require a postmortem with at least one cross-team reviewer and owner timelines tracked in the corrective actions table.
- This runbook should be exercised at least twice per year via game days.

Contact and escalation directory:
- Platform SRE oncall: pager +1-555-0101, Slack @platform-oncall
- Runtime service owner: @runtime-team
- CSR lead: csr@redwood.com

End of document.
